- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast 3–5 days ahead, targeting 1–2% below recent high.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates in early horizon (days 1–7) when sentiment is volatile; reduce first 3–5 days by 1–2%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or negative sentiment, model underperforms; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days to compensate for low confidence.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model often fails to account for mean reversion; reduce forecast by 0.5–1% every 3–5 days after peak.
